facts.text: SpaceX and Tesla have formed special committees of independent directors to explore a potential combination, CEO of both companies Elon Musk said on Tuesday during SpaceX's third-quarter earnings call amid heightened market speculation.
"It is an odd kabuki dance where two groups of people are talking and I cannot be in the conversation," Musk said.
He cautioned against assuming a deal is inevitable.

To buy SpaceX, Tesla would have to create millions of new stock shares, which for current Tesla owners would mean owning a smaller slice of a much larger pie.
SpaceX’s launch goals require tens of billions of dollars every year — extra spending that could drain Tesla’s ability to build new car factories and battery plants.
That said, most Wall Street analysts and legal experts believe SpaceX would acquire Tesla (or absorb it through a stock swap) rather than vice versa.
